dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: *sigh* My brother's right. I'm a writer of books, but no seller of them...

choices.text: What are you working on right now?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Just about, only a few chapters left. It's just... Could I ask you a question?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: How much do you think my calligraphy could sell for?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There are some things money can't buy!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Oh, come on, what's with that old-fashioned talk? I'm being serious here.

choices.text: I don't know much about the calligraphy market.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Phew... Thank you. At least you're not couching it in business jargon like they do at home. "Penned words are worth their weight in gold," and "there's no market for such prices as you might command"...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Earlier, I asked my brother about the typewriter situation. He cut me off just as I was about to ask why he hadn't brought one back for me, and can you guess what he said?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That he didn't bring one back on purpose?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: No. In fact, he'd actually bought one back a long time ago. He even knows about everything that's happened recently, and asked me to try the typewriter to see if the size was appropriate.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: As it turns out, it did — in fact, its dimensions had been modified to suit the dimensions of my palms, which made it very comfortable to use.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: He even said that, in an emergency, I could use this typewriter for my novels and other writing needs, and that he'd already notified my great-grandfather of the arrangement.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: As to why he didn't just give me the typewriter earlier... It was actually because he was hoping that I could eventually improve my penmanship.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: They say that "to see a person's writing is to see them also." Hand-written words will always give a reader a greater sense of closeness to the author.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: My brother said that he was also willing to part with the "Chronicle of Cleansing Ink" rather than sending me the typewriter straightaway...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: ...Because he felt that while my handwriting wasn't up to par, it still showed a sense of remarkable style and vigor.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: As such, he feared that were I to simply keep using a typewriter, I would forget how to write with a pen altogether, thus ending any possibility for my improvement in calligraphy.

choices.text: Huh, and I thought he'd say...

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: To be honest, he had me sweating there too. I was so nervous, I almost crushed my teacup.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I was afraid he might say something like: "In business, closeness is communication, communication is connection, and connection is Mora — as such, to practice one's penmanship is to earn Mora."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: If he had said that, I would've had to flee to Chongyun's place and stay there for... maybe ten days to two weeks.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, he seems like a reasonable fellow, then.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Yeah. He never talks about the business with me. He just lets me... live my life.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: But... *sigh* Even though he says nothing about it, we have too many business dealings for me to not know that "to see a person's writing is to see them also, and fine words written are worth their weight in gold"?

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: A single article of my great-grandfather's writing is worth hundreds of thousands of Mora, and a letter from my brother can bring someone here just to say a personal "thank you."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: When I went out with my brother on a courtesy call, I even saw someone who had hung and framed a congratulatory note left by my great-grandfather.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Now take a look at these books. These are novels I just wrote, and the contents are completely identical.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: But when I signed one of them, the last stroke I penned went a few inches wide, and voila — it can sell for two hundred extra Mora.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: The words are all the same, and the writing hadn't changed one bit, either. But the price changed, all on account of the length of a single stroke.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Congratulatory notes can have the same content, but everyone would hang my great-grandfather's up on a wall, and carefully preserve one that my brother sent.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I know that these are just trivial matters of business, and no one really cares what the letters themselves say — it's all about who sent it to them. It's just...

choices.text: I remember every letter you've ever written to me.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I know. Thank you. I know it's been tough on you, reading my scribblings. I'll learn how to use that typewriter as soon as possible. We shall soon be forever rid of badly-written letters!

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: Pfft... Haha! Alright, alright. In that case, I shall continue writing to you in my finest illegible "calligraphy."

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: But should you ever find my lettering neat and orderly, please do come find me as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I may have been kidnapped — or perhaps I just really want to see you.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: #Ah, would you look at that, it's getting late. I shall see you later, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Xingqiu
response.text: I wonder if Mr. Xifan also turned to the sword because he did not want to see the products of his pen peddled for coin...

choices.text: You call them scribbles, but I call them heartfelt.
See, I've got them all right here. Well-kept, too.
That hand-written work was more valuable.
But I enjoy every word you pen.
